title: Triara - I scrapped half my browser game and turned it into a fantasy team manager
author: juanludlf
selftext:
Hey all. I'm a solo dev and Triara is a hobby project I've been making since March, just for fun. Play here -> [https://triara.io](https://triara.io)

  
I built most of it with AI-assisted coding (opus 5.5). I used it mainly for prototyping systems, iterating on UI/gameplay ideas and replacing chunks of the original codebase as the game evolved.

The biggest lesson for me was that AI made adding features very fast, but it also made it dangerously easy to keep expanding a bad foundation. At some point I realized I was patching the original game instead of improving it, so I scrapped a large part of it and rebuilt the core around the team-management loop.

It started as a MyBrute tribute, grew into a full RPG, and last week I realised the only part I really enjoyed was building a team and watching it fight. So I cut the rest and made it a manager.

* You don't fight. You sign champions, pick three starters, and the battles play out on their own.
* There's a league match every day, and you know tomorrow's opponent in advance. Top 3 go up at the end of the season and bottom 3 go down.
* There's a knockout cup every weekend.
* Every champion belongs to somebody. If you want another player's star, you pay their release clause. Champions also draw wages, so a squad you can't afford starts to fall apart.
* Tactics happen before kickoff: sun, moon and tide work like rock-paper-scissors, so you can set your lineup to counter tomorrow's opponent.

It's free and runs in the browser at **triara.io**. It's a hobby project, so expect bugs. I'd love to know whether the daily league keeps you coming back or starts to feel like a chore.
